content.text:
“Clean gold” is often called **24-karat gold** or **fine gold**, and it is usually labeled **99.9% pure** because, in practice, it is extremely difficult and costly to make gold absolutely 100.000% pure.

The remaining **0.1%** is made up of **trace impurities**, such as tiny amounts of silver, copper, platinum-group metals, or other elements that remain after refining.

A few key points:

- **99.9% gold** means **999 parts gold out of 1,000**.
- It is commonly written as **999 fine gold**.
- This is considered commercially “pure” gold.
- Truly **100% pure gold** is more of a theoretical ideal than a practical standard, because even highly refined gold contains microscopic impurities.
- Some gold is refined even further, such as **99.99%** or **99.999%**, but it requires more advanced refining and is more expensive.

So clean gold is called **99.9% pure** because that level is high enough to be considered pure for most bullion, jewelry, and investment purposes, while acknowledging that a tiny amount of impurity remains.
